title: The Dasam Granth today
hookLine: it is installed at Takht Hazur Sahib and Takht Patna Sahib, and read by Sikhs

lines: BEFORE SUNRISE, A SMALL PRAYER BOOK.
WHERE DOES THE BOOK LIVE NOW?
cards: Before sunrise, in a Sikh home, someone sits with a small prayer book wrapped in cloth.
They recite Guru Nanak's Japji, then keep going into words of the Tenth Guru: the Jaap Sahib, a long rush of praise, then a set of swayyas, a different set from the thirty-three met earlier.
Some of that morning comes from a book this path has spent weeks in, the Dasam Granth. So where does that book live now, outside the prayer book in someone's lap?

teach.h: TWO TAKHTS: HIS BIRTH, HIS LAST DAYS.
teach.b: Start with two places. One is Nanded, two days back, where Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib stands. The other is Patna, far to the east, where tradition says the Tenth Guru was born, and where Takht Sri Patna Sahib stands.
A Takht is a throne, a seat of authority in Sikh life. At both of these Takhts, the Dasam Granth is installed, given a place of honor, and read, alongside the Guru Granth Sahib.
So the Tenth Guru's book is honored in a special way at the two places that hold his beginning and his end. Next, the daily prayers.

teach.h: IN THE MORNING AND EVENING PRAYERS.
teach.b: The Sikh Rehat Maryada, the shared code of conduct, lists the morning prayers, the Nitnem. Alongside Guru Nanak's Japji, it names compositions from the Dasam Granth: the Jaap Sahib and the swayyas.
In the evening prayer there's the Chaupai, a prayer for protection.

And at the Amrit ceremony, when Sikhs are initiated into the Khalsa, the Jaap Sahib, the swayyas and the Chaupai are among the prayers recited over the sweetened water, alongside hymns of the Guru Granth Sahib.

teach.h: HONORED, BUT NOT THE GURU'S SEAT.
teach.b: So the book isn't only on a high seat. It's in mouths and mornings. Third, a careful distinction Sikhs keep.
The Guru Granth Sahib is the Guru.
The Dasam Granth is honored, read and recited, but it is not the Guru. Holding both, honor without confusing the two, is part of how Sikhs live with this book today.
Read and honored: two different things, and both true at once.

how: Sikhs who keep the Nitnem recite the Jaap Sahib and swayyas in the morning and the Chaupai in the evening, and the Dasam Granth is installed and read at Takht Hazur Sahib and Takht Patna Sahib.

games.q: what does “the dasam granth today” mean?
o: the new name of the Guru Granth Sahib today
the Tenth Guru's book, honored but not the Guru
a modern book that replaced the old prayers

games.q: where the book lives: tap the pairs.
p: where tradition says he was born
a prayer for protection in the evening

s: the Tenth Guru's words are only read by scholars
the Jaap Sahib, the swayyas and the Chaupai are part of the daily prayers.
the Dasam Granth is installed at two Takhts
at Hazur Sahib and Patna Sahib, alongside the Guru Granth Sahib.
in gurdwaras the Dasam Granth takes the Guru's seat
the Guru Granth Sahib is the Guru. the Dasam Granth is honored and read, without that place.

games.q: you want to hear the Tenth Guru's words every day, without traveling. where do you find them?
o: in the Nitnem, the daily prayers.
games.why: the Sikh Rehat Maryada lists the Jaap Sahib and the swayyas among the morning prayers, and the Chaupai in the evening.

practice: Picture one Takht, Hazur Sahib on the Godavari, Patna Sahib in the east, or the Akal Takht in Amritsar facing the Golden Temple, and the people walking in this morning, covering their heads and bowing.
Rest with that image, and if you pray, join their morning in your own words.

wordCard.voice: The Dasam Granth today. Installed at Takht Hazur Sahib and Takht Patna Sahib, recited in daily prayers and at the Amrit ceremony, honored alongside the Guru Granth Sahib. Today's word.

orig.note: Punjabi: a throne; in Sikh life, a seat of authority.

carryVoice: Your line: read and honored. Kept on a high seat, and alive in ordinary mornings. Until tomorrow.
